chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends to create the Imam from the Imam, He sends an angel. So he takes a draught from water beneath the Throne, then casts it, or delivers it, to the Imam, and he drinks it. Then he remains in the womb for forty days, not hearing speech; then after that he hears speech. Then when his mother gives birth to him, Allah sends to him that angel who took the draught, and he writes upon his right upper arm:”
“And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none to alter His words.”
Then when he rises with this matter, Allah raises for him in every town a beacon by which he looks upon the deeds of the servants.”

key_terms.الرَّحِمِ: the womb, where the Imam remains for forty days in the described state
key_terms.الشَّرْبَةَ: a draught or drink taken from the water beneath the Throne
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader being described in the narration
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, mentioned here as the place beneath which the water is taken from
key_terms.كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ: the Word of your Lord, cited in the Qur'anic phrase written upon him
key_terms.مَلَكًا: an angel sent by Allah to carry out a role in the Imam’s creation and designation
key_terms.مَنَارًا: a beacon or sign by which the Imam looks upon the deeds of the servants

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the divine creation and designation of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the divinely ordained creation and designation of the Imam, portraying his origin, recognition, and special awareness as matters established by Allah عزّ وجلّ. It also cites a Qur'anic phrase to express the truth and justice of the divine word, presenting the Imamate as part of Allah’s unwavering decree.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Yunus Bin Zabyan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, whenever He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends to Create the Imam<sup>asws</sup> from the Imams<sup>asws</sup>, Sends an Angel. So he takes a drink from the water beneath the Throne, then casts it, or hands it over to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> drinks it, and he<sup>asws</sup> stays in the womb for forty days, not hearing the speech. Then he<sup>asws</sup> hears the speech after that. So when his<sup>asws</sup> mother places him<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sends that Angel to him, the one who took the drink, and he writes upon his right arm:
[6:115] And the Word of your Lord has been accomplished truly and justly; there is none who can change His Words’.
So when he<sup>asws</sup> does stand with this command, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Raises for him<sup>asws</sup> a beacon in every city. He<sup>asws</sup> can look with this to the deeds of the servants’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadidfrom Mansur ibn Yunus from Yunus ibn Zabyan who has said the following.

“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say, ‘When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, decides to create the Imam from another Imam He sends an angel with a drink of water from under the Throne. Then the angel would make the Imam to drink it and would give it to him to drink. For the first forty days he would not hear any words and thereafter he would hear words. When his mogthor would give birth Aallah would send the same angel who had brought the water. The angels would on his right should, “
. .in all truth and justice, your Lord’s Word has been completed. No one can change His Words. He is All-hearing and All-knowing.”. [6:115]
When he would rise to execute the task of an Imam Allah would raise a light house for him in every town through which he would examine the deeds of the servants of Allah.”
